question: Should exact requester consumption of descendant output count as terminal descendant-delivery proof before the requester's final outward cron send succeeds?
rationale: The patch can mechanically record the event, but only maintainers can decide whether requester consumption or final user-visible delivery is the intended product boundary for suppressing descendant retry and failure finalization.

options.title: Accept after live proof
options.body: Accept the narrow requester-consumption boundary after redacted runtime and restart evidence proves only explicitly consumed descendants become delivered while all others remain retryable.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Keep descendant rows pending until the requester result is successfully delivered outward, even when the requester already incorporated their output.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox
options.body: Pause this PR and handle consumed and unconsumed completions together in the broader durable completion inbox or spool design.

recommendation.title: Accept after live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow requester-consumption boundary after redacted runtime and restart evidence proves only explicitly consumed descendants become delivered while all others remain retryable.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent-history routing candidate across the central cron fallback and persisted registry surfaces affected by this semantic choice.
